Dear Shri, Dubey, 
 
 
As you are aware, the President prescribes the form in which the accounts of the 
Union and of the States are to be kept, on the advice of the Comprtoller and Auditor General 
of India. These constitutional provisions have further been elucidated in the Government 
Accountin Rules, 1990 which state that the ' Form' also includes the prescriptions not only of 
the broad from in which the accounts are to be kept but also the basis for appropriate heads 
under which the transactions are to be classified. In the existing 6 tiers classifications 
structure consisting of Major Head, Sub Major Head, Minor Head, Sub Head, Detailed Head 
and Object Head, the State Governments with effects from January 1982 have been entrusted 
with their consent , the functions of the Central Government in so far as these relate to 
opening of subheads and below in the State concerned. The comptroller and Auditor General 
of India also has delegated to the State Accounts  General  the power to give advice to the 
State/Union Territory Government in the matter of opening subhead and below in their 
accounts, which instructions were endorsed to State Chief Secretary vide this office General 
Circular No-2 AC/1982 No. 45-AC/12-77 dated  18 January, 1982  (for states) and General 
Circular No- 34-AC/1982 No-536-AC/12-77 dated 9 june, 1982 (for U.Ts). 
 
 
According to the extant procedure, the State Government is required to seek 
the mandatory advice of the Local Accounts General (A&E) in the matter of opening of 
subheads and below. We, however, find that this requirement is not being obeserved and the 
advice of State Accountant General (A&E) is not being sought for before opening subheads 
below by the State Government. This is at variance with the constitutional requirements. This 
creates accounting complications too.

subheads. etc. may please be routed through the Finance Department (Budget Wing) in the
